title: Maudrin's Dissent
author: Maudrin the Lampwright
pages: To the Archwright Isthenne and the Nine Lenses, I, Maudrin, Lampwright of the order, set down my dissent, so that it stands in the record when the record is all that remains.
You say the night is a cruelty, and that if we draw the Dawn-Star down to burn beneath the world we will end it forever. I say the night is a border, and you do not know what it holds back.
You have measured her orbit and her heat. You have not asked her. We would take a star from the sky because we are afraid of the dark. That is not wisdom. It is a child's terror with a ladder.
If she falls, she will not fall gently. If she burns beneath the world, the world will have a wound, and wounds are where things get in. I will not cut the Lantern-runes. Strike my name if you must.
In the margin, a later hand: Maudrin was right. Maudrin gave her soul to the Lanterns with the rest of us. Her name was not struck. It is the first one on the pillar.
